method: Ran the exact three Python fences and six-assertion W6 verifier. Compared all demo stdout with the published text blocks; exercised forged-tenant, missing-scope, malformed JSON, extra-field, blank-query, and non-object input paths before credential lookup. Reviewed the current OWASP Secrets Management, Logging, Authorization Cheat Sheets and AWS Well-Architected SEC02-BP03. No provider request or external network call.
limitations: The local fixtures prove only behavior of constructed objects and the in-memory fake broker/upstream; they do not verify production traces, log sinks, secret managers, sandboxing, or provider retention.
The first fixture deliberately constructs a tool-call object that already contains a synthetic secret. A schema field name alone does not establish that a credential value was sent to a model.
The demonstration uses synthetic test strings only; no real credentials were read or used.
Authorization behavior in a live identity provider, tenant-aware secret broker, and downstream service remains untested.
